pi.name: John Schiefelbein
pi.title: Professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
pi.bio: John Schiefelbein received his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin at Madison in 1987 and completed postdoctoral work at Michigan State University (1987-1989). He received a National Science Foundation Young Investigator Award in 1992. His laboratory studies root epidermis development in the flowering plant Arabidopsis thaliana as a model for understanding how distinct cell fates arise during the development of multicellular organisms.

lab_description: The Schiefelbein Lab seeks to understand the molecular mechanisms that enable distinct cell fates to arise during the development of multicellular organisms. The lab focuses on the specification and patterning of hair and non-hair cells in the root epidermis of Arabidopsis thaliana, a simple tissue containing only two cell types in which cells make a binary developmental decision based on their position relative to underlying cortical cells. Arabidopsis offers rapidly observable root development, a simple tissue structure, genetic tractability, and a fully sequenced genome. The lab uses molecular genetic approaches, including mutant analysis, tissue-specific transcript profiling, and single-cell RNA sequencing, and extends its comparative work on root and root-hair development across the plant kingdom.

research_areas.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing in plants
research_areas.summary: The lab has adapted scRNA-seq to individual plant cells, revealing gene expression from single Arabidopsis root cells and providing insight into cellular heterogeneity, rare cell types, and developmental trajectories. Work continues on expanding applications of this method in plants.

research_areas.title: Root and root-hair development programs across the plant kingdom
research_areas.summary: Using available plant genome sequences, the lab performs comparative transcript profiling of developing roots and root hairs across diverse plant species to identify conserved and divergent gene expression programs.

research_areas.title: Cell-type pattern formation in the root epidermis
research_areas.summary: The lab investigates the molecular mechanisms that determine root epidermal cell patterning in Arabidopsis and other species, including how regulatory proteins interact, when developmental mechanisms are activated, the evolutionary origins of the patterning system, and the downstream factors in the gene regulatory network.
